prox.name: Front proximity sensors
prox.tip: Black, shiny or transparent objects reflect little infrared and look further away than they are. Test against the obstacles you will actually use.

proxback.name: Back proximity sensors
proxback.tip: Useful for detecting a robot following behind you in swarm experiments.

ground.name: Ground sensors
ground.range: High on white, low on black (about 0–1000)
ground.tip: For line following use high-contrast tape on a matte floor. Calibrate thresholds on the arena floor itself, not on a desk.

buttons.name: Touch buttons
buttons.summary: 5 capacitive buttons: forward, backward, left, right, centre
buttons.event: onevent buttons · 20 Hz, or onevent button.center (etc.) on change
buttons.tip: Holding the centre button for 3 seconds switches the robot off, so don't use a long centre press as an input.

motors.name: Wheels and motors
motors.tip: Equal targets rarely give a perfectly straight line. Hair and dust on the wheels are the usual cause of drift; clean them before blaming your code.

leds.name: LEDs
leds.summary: 39 LEDs in total, including RGB top and bottom LEDs
leds.tip: Giving each robot a colour by state is the cheapest debugging tool you have, and it shows up well in video recordings.

inside.name: Internal sensors
inside.range: acc −32 to 32 (1 g ≈ 23) · temperature in 0.1 °C · mic 0–255
inside.event: onevent acc · 16 Hz · onevent tap · onevent mic
inside.tip: The accelerometer detects bumps and lifts. Set mic.threshold before relying on onevent mic in a noisy lab.

sound.name: Speaker and IR remote receiver
sound.summary: Speaker; infrared receiver for RC5 remote controls
sound.code: call sound.freq(Hz, duration) · call sound.system(n) · rc5.command
sound.tip: Turn sounds off in shared sessions; ten beeping robots make the lab unusable for everyone else.

usb.name: USB port and battery
usb.summary: Micro-USB for data and charging; built-in LiPo battery
usb.range: A few hours of driving per charge
usb.tip: Many cheap cables are charge-only and the robot won't be detected. Keep one known data cable marked at the lab bench.
